summary: Partial header/body truncation at edge -> GPU worker hang and cascading 5xx wave
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13T20:10Z we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx errors from the API gateway for a subset of small-payload streaming and short-chat requests. Impact: multiple enterprise tenants (notably Nimbus Retail) saw request failures and degraded throughput for chat and embedding calls; dashboard shows 5xx rate increased from baseline 0.4% to 8% in us-east-1 over a 35m window. Environment: prod, us-east-1, mixed streaming + embed workload, canary routing disabled.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send many concurrent short streaming requests (20-50ms prompt + small context) using HTTP2 multiplexing and keepalives; 2) Observe a small portion of connections where the upstream runtime receives truncated header/body (Content-Length mismatch or partial header frames) and returns an error path; 3) GPU worker that processes the stream enters a halted state (kernel spin) and watchdog eventually kills the worker, causing upstream 5xx + connection resets.

Observed logs / symptoms: apigw logs show repeated 502/503 with upstream reset and "upstream prematurely closed connection". Edge proxy (envoy) traces show occasional "header frame truncated" and "HTTP2 RST_STREAM (2)". Serving runtime logs capture a thread blocked in NVML memory slot allocation with stack trace pointing at kv-cache restore path; watchdog logs show repeated SIGTERM -> respawn. No initial OOM recorded on host; GPU metrics show short lived NVML timeouts preceding worker hang.

Impact to customer: degraded UX for chat sessions, some lost streaming frames, and elevated retry churn increasing request latency across the board.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 20:05Z - first small uptick in 5xx; 20:12Z - clear elevation; 20:25Z - mitigation (rate limiting) partially reduces volume but errors persist; 20:50Z - rollback candidate config applied on a subset of edge nodes.

Hypotheses considered: (1) Recent edge header buffer tuning (PR #2103) reduced max header buffer sizes leading to partial header/frame truncation on a subset of HTTP2 clients -> malformed requests hit an error path in the runtime; (2) Malformed request handling in runtime triggers an unexpected code path that races with kv-cache restore and can spin GPU worker threads (NVML calls) causing watchdog to kill the process; (3) Keepalive reuse/HTTP2 windowing combined with the header truncation increased accept-queue backpressure and amplified the failure.

Evidence: The only recent deploy touching edge proxies was PR 2103 (header buffer sizing). Correlation between edge nodes with that config and error rate is strong (95th percentile of 5xx concentrated on nodes with new buffers). Runtime stack traces during hang reference kv-cache CRC validation code executed just after request parse.

Investigations in progress: full core capture on affected runtime instances; reproduce with a test client that intentionally sends split header frames to trigger truncation; review NVML logs for persistent timeout pattern.

Related artifacts: trace ids: trace-us-east-20260313-20-az3-[redacted]; runtime core: s3://redwood-runtime-cores/us-east/2026-03-13/core-479001.tar.gz (restricted).

mitigation_and_workaround:
1) Immediate: rolled back header-buffer sizing change on edge nodes in us-east-1 (partial roll back) which reduced newly-injected malformed frames; 2) Applied temporary strict request validation at API gateway to reject truncated frames early (reject + 400) to avoid hitting runtime error path; 3) Applied soft rate-limit for short streaming requests for affected tenants.

Customer communication: Notified Nimbus Retail via support channel with status and temporary mitigation; recommending they avoid large concurrent short-stream bursts until we confirm full remediation.
next_steps:
1) Finish core analysis and upload sanitized backtrace to ticket (ENG). 2) Add guard in serving-runtime request-parsing to gracefully drop malformed HTTP2 frames before kv-cache restore. 3) Create automated test that fuzzes split header frames and run against canary edge + runtime. 4) Roll an edge config verification job to ensure buffer sizes are aligned between edge and internal proxies. 5) Post-incident: postmortem and runbook update.

Owners: Edge team (Carlos Mendoza) for config verification; Runtime team (Emily Zhang) for parsing guard and core analysis; SRE (Liam O'Connor) for rollout and autoscale knobs.
resolution: Work is ongoing. Partial rollback + request-validation reduced error rate from 8% back to 0.9% by 2026-03-14 03:00Z. Runtime patch for graceful malformed-frame handling is in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2210 and under test in staging. Full resolution pending runtime patch and coordinated canary rollout.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer Nimbus reported intermittent streaming failures starting ~20:10Z; opened incident and escalated to SRE.
SRE (Liam): Confirmed 5xx spike in us-east-1 apigw metrics. Correlated to edge nodes on canary config. Initiated partial rollback at 20:50Z.
Edge Eng (Carlos): PR 2103 adjusted http2 header buffer thresholds to reduce memory pressure; suspect smaller buffers caused split-frame reassembly mismatches with some client stacks.
Runtime Eng (Emily): Collected core dumps from runtime-37. Initial stack shows NVML calls in kv-cache restore path. Working on repro harness that sends intentionally-split headers.
Support (Aisha): Notified Nimbus CSM with initial mitigation steps and recommended rate limiting on their side for short bursts. Customer acknowledged and provided request samples.
SRE (Liam): Applied temporary request validation rule at the apigw layer to reject truncated frames; monitoring for collateral impact.
Edge Eng (Carlos): Preparing automated config check to ensure edge and internal proxies share identical HTTP2 reassembly params prior to any future edge tuning.
Runtime Eng (Emily): Drafted a small defensive fix to early-validate header frames before touching kv-cache; shipping to staging for smoke tests (PR 2210).
SRE (Liam): Will follow up with full postmortem and SLA impact calculation once runtime patch is verified.
